question_text: Find the derivative of x sin x from the first principle with respect to x.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — say how you break the numerator into two parts and what each part gives.

steps.label: State the first principle
steps.margin_note: First mark. Both factors change when x becomes x + h — the x in front and the angle inside the sine. Substitute into both.
lines: (the definition of the derivative from the first principle)

recall.must_convey: That the first principle is written with f(x) = x sin x and f(x + h) = (x + h) sin(x + h).
accept: write the first principle with f of x equal to x sin x
f of x plus h is x plus h into sin of x plus h
substitute x plus h in both the front factor and the angle
first principle rasta, x plus h into sin x plus h ani rasta
take the limit of the difference quotient
heard_as: x plus h into sin x plus h

steps.why: The definition is the marked move. This is a product of two functions, so x + h has to replace x in both of them, not only inside the sine.
common_mistakes: Substituting x + h into the sine only and leaving the front factor as x.
Using the product rule, which is not a first-principle answer.
steps.memory_tip: Replace x by x + h in every place x appears, front factor included.

steps.label: Split the numerator in two
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Expanding (x + h) sin(x + h) is what separates the two pieces. In the second piece the h cancels the h below at once, so it needs no identity at all.
lines: (x + h) sin(x + h) = x sin(x + h) + h sin(x + h)

lines.text: (subtract x sin x: x sin(x + h) − x sin x

lines: x[sin(x + h) − sin x] + h sin(x + h)

recall.must_convey: That (x + h) sin(x + h) is expanded and regrouped as x[sin(x + h) − sin x] + h sin(x + h).
accept: expand x plus h into sin x plus h and group the two x terms
the numerator is x times the difference of sines plus h sin x plus h
the h in the second part cancels the h in the denominator
bracket expand cheste rendu parts vasthayi
break it into a sine difference part and a leftover part

steps.why: Split this way, one piece carries a difference of sines that the identity handles and the other has its h cancel straight away. Both then have limits that can be read off.
common_mistakes: Splitting as x sin x + h sin h, which is not what (x + h) sin(x + h) expands to.
Writing the second piece as sin x instead of sin(x + h).
steps.memory_tip: Expand the bracket, then group the two x terms together and leave the h term on its own.
lines_compact: (x + h) sin(x + h) = x sin(x + h) + h sin(x + h)
x[sin(x + h) − sin x] + h sin(x + h)

steps.label: Use sin C − sin D
steps.margin_note: Third mark. The 2 in front of the identity is exactly what turns (sin(h/2))/h into (sin(h/2))/(h/2), so the standard limit applies with nothing left over.

lines.text: (sin C − sin D = 2 cos((C + D)/2) sin((C − D)/2),
with C = x + h and D = x)

recall.must_convey: That sin(x + h) − sin x = 2 cos(x + h/2) sin(h/2), and the 2 makes the denominator h/2 so the standard limit applies.
accept: use sin c minus sin d to get two cos of x plus h by two into sin h by two
the two in front makes the denominator h by two
sin h by two over h by two tends to one
sin minus sin formula apply cheste two cos sin vasthundi
apply the sum to product formula to the sine difference

steps.why: The sine angle is h/2, not h, so the denominator has to become h/2 as well. The 2 that the identity produces does exactly that, with no extra factor to carry.
common_mistakes: Halving the first angle too and writing cos(x/2 + h/2).
steps.memory_tip: The 2 from sin C − sin D pairs with the h/2 inside the sine. Together they make the standard limit exact.

steps.label: Take the limit
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Both pieces contribute: x cos x from the sine difference and sin x from the leftover term. Dropping the second is the usual loss here.
lines: f′(x) = x cos x + sin x

recall.must_convey: That the two limits give x cos x and sin x, so the answer is sin x + x cos x.
accept: the answer is sin x plus x cos x
the first part gives x cos x and the second gives sin x
derivative of x sin x is sin x plus x cos x
sin x plus x cos x answer vasthundi
both parts contribute one term each
heard_as: sin x plus x cos x

steps.why: The answer matches the product rule result, which is the check worth making: the first principle must reproduce it, and here it does.
common_mistakes: Giving x cos x only and losing the sin x term.
Giving cos x + x sin x, with the two functions swapped.
steps.memory_tip: Two pieces, two terms: sin x from the leftover part, x cos x from the sine difference.
lines_compact: f′(x) = x cos x + sin x

insider_note: Split (x + h)sin(x + h) into x sin(x + h) + h sin(x + h) so the two standard pieces separate. One gives x cos x and the other sin x.
